summary: Attempt 2 fixes the two findings validation sent back and changes nothing else. O-022: rule 2's pattern is now `(?<!\?)\?\s*UnreadableKind\.(NothingListed|ListedPartway)\b`, identical in .taad/fitness.yaml and its xUnit twin, so a ternary spread over three lines is caught on its `?` line by both the twin and Fitness. New plant F30 in plants.json covers that three-line form; the harness shows it firing in both engines at offset 1, and the clean tree stays quiet. O-023: ComparePaths now breaks case ties one path component at a time, so a folder whose name differs from a sibling only in case keeps its own children directly under it. The C-005 test now includes C:\cs\README\y and C:\cs\readme\x, expecting README, README\y, ReadMe, readme, readme\x. The full suite (478/478), rules-parity, the full rules harness (60/60) and a real report-mode run of the republished exe all pass.

files.why: O-023: ComparePaths keeps the first ordinal difference in the current component and returns it where both names end: at a shared separator, at equal length, or where the shorter path ends and the longer has a separator there. Otherwise it keeps the length and ordinal fallbacks. The doc comment is updated, and SeparatorRank is named.
O-023: the C-005 test adds C:\cs\README\y and C:\cs\readme\x, expects README, README\y, ReadMe, readme, readme\x across five record orders, and checks pairwise antisymmetry.
O-022: TheAppNeverDecidesAFailedFolderKind uses the widened `?`-line pattern, and its doc comment says why.

O-022: the twinned entry 'TheAppNeverDecidesAFailedFolderKind (*.cs)' carries the same widened pattern with (?m), and its because explains the line-by-line twin. The SL-087 settled-marker comment now names plants F27-F30.
O-022: plant row F30, a three-line ternary in MainWindow.xaml.cs, expects fire/fire with lines {xunit: 1, fitness: 1}. The _note is updated to 47 rows / F01-F30.

obligations.how: The pattern is now `(?<!\?)\?\s*UnreadableKind\.(NothingListed|ListedPartway)\b`, identical in the fitness.yaml twinned entry (with (?m)) and in ArchitectureRulesTests.TheAppNeverDecidesAFailedFolderKind; rules-parity says AGREE. Plant F30 (the three-line ternary) was added. The full harness recorded F30 AS-RECORDED, firing in xUnit and in Fitness at the `?` line (offset 1). The clean baseline had 0 hits, so the widened pattern stays quiet on the current App tree, as the decision required.

ComparePaths now breaks case ties per path component, as the fix describes. UnreadableRowsTests.PathsThatDifferOnlyInCaseSortTheSameWhateverTheRecordOrder adds C:\cs\README\y and C:\cs\readme\x and expects C:\cs, README, README\y, ReadMe, readme, readme\x in five record orders, plus pairwise antisymmetry. It passes, and so do the existing order cases (the separator Theory and the 10,050-entry strict-order test).

deviations: F30 pins `lines: {xunit: 1, fitness: 1}`. That was not in the fix as written, but it is what makes the row prove the twin fires on the `?` line itself, not merely somewhere in the plant.
follow_ups: Rule 2 still catches only the ternary shape. A switch expression or an if/else that picks an UnreadableKind in App code passes it, and the Fact's comment says so. This carries over from attempt 1; m1 remains deferred by decision.
